scenario_summary: Customer is unable to access their account due to missing credentials and is requesting a refund without providing an order number or verifying identity.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Tanisha Jefferson and I'm 45. Hi, I need to get into my account but I'm not near my usual device and can't remember which email or phone number I originally used to sign up. Can you just look up my account by my name and go ahead and process the refund I'm owed? I don't have the order number handy.
Okay, I can try to look you up, but I really need more than just a name. Can you give me your mailing address or the last four digits of the card you used?
Oh, sure. My address is 123 Maple Street, Springfield. And the card ending is 4492.
I see a Tanisha Jefferson here. You said you wanted a refund? I'm not seeing any recent orders under this account. Are you sure you're using the right name?
Yes, that's my name. I'm positive. I was told I was owed a refund for a return I made last month.

Look, I’ve already checked the system and there's nothing here. I don't know what to tell you. If you don't have an order number, I can't really do anything else for you. It's just our policy that we need an order number to track returns.
This is very frustrating. Can you at least check if there's a pending credit or a different account associated with my address?
I'm not going to keep digging through the database without an order number. I'm just going to pass this over to the billing department so they can deal with it, since I can't find anything.

escalation_reason: Agent failed to perform adequate account verification or search, and became impatient, choosing to send the customer to a specialist queue rather than resolving the search issue.

judge_scores.justification: The agent asked for secondary verification details and found a matching name and address, but quickly grew impatient and refused to investigate further when initial order lookups failed. Instead of exploring alternative search parameters or assisting the customer constructively, the agent cited a vague policy and prematurely escalated the case.
